smells.finding: Measured with an AST pass over checks.py rather than eyeballed: the longest function body is refs_line_self_consistent at 31 code lines (docstrings excluded), then inbound_attribution at 27 and run at 25. Every other function is 14 code lines or fewer. refs_line_self_consistent's 31 lines are one flat loop with six independent arithmetic rules, one branch each; splitting them into helpers would scatter arithmetic that has to be read together. No long method.

MapUnderCheck spans 98 lines but holds 12 members, none longer than 7 code lines, all of one responsibility: read the built map the way a reader gets it. StoreScan is one __init__ of 10 code lines. Neither is a god class.

refs_line_self_consistent and inbound_attribution each carry the same unparsable-line branch, including the message text verbatim: f"{where}: cannot read the inbound line: {line!r}". Minor and low-risk -- the FORMAT knowledge itself is correctly centralised in the REFS_* constants and parse_refs, which the module documents as 'the ONE place that knows how a page spells its inbound references'. Raised as an observation, not a blocker: two copies of a one-line failure message do not threaten the gate's property.

The six check functions read almost exclusively off the MapUnderCheck they are handed, which reads like envy at a glance. It is not: MapUnderCheck is a data holder built for exactly this, and the checks are free functions precisely so the CHECKS registry can enumerate them by name and run() can report per-check. Making them methods would couple the registry to the class and lose the per-check naming the failure output depends on.

(root, artifacts, out) travels together through cli -> run() -> MapUnderCheck.__init__ and again through _build_into. MapUnderCheck is the object that already collapses that clump, so run() re-expands a triple it immediately re-packs on its first line. Cosmetic; the CLI boundary legitimately deals in three separate paths. Observation only.

The supplement key is a 'module:name' string and checks.py picks it apart with .split(":", 1) in six places, twice welded to a further .rsplit(".", 1)[-1] to reach the leaf. The module/name/leaf decomposition is a real domain concept with no type. A small Key namedtuple with .module/.name/.leaf would remove six ad-hoc splits and make entity_symbol_join's leaf-only comparison self-documenting rather than a comment. Raised as an observation and an out-of-scope candidate: the store schema is strings and gate g3 owns it, so changing it here would widen scope.
Widest signature is three parameters (run, MapUnderCheck.__init__, _build_into). Nothing near a parameter-object threshold.

Tested by attack rather than by reading. A5 respelled the rendered inbound line and the blast radius was exactly the four REFS_* constants plus parse_refs -- the module's stated design goal ('a later gate that respells it updates this and nothing else') held under a real mutation. The one genuinely cross-cutting change a later gate makes, an added index tier, lands on the single named constant TOP_INDEX_PAGES.

checks.py has two axes of change -- what is checked, and how a page is spelled -- but the second is confined to the REFS_* block and title_key, so the two axes do not tangle. No evidence a later gate has to touch unrelated parts of the file to move one of them.

entity_symbol_join builds both sides of its comparison with chains over primitives: key.split(":", 1)[1].rsplit(".", 1)[-1] and symbol.split(":", 1)[-1].rsplit(".", 1)[-1]. This is the same defect as primitive-obsession above and the same fix removes both; recorded separately because Fowler treats them separately. Observation, folded into the same out-of-scope candidate.

Nothing unused ships. The CHECKS registry has six real members and run() is its only consumer. MAX_REPORTED and TOP_INDEX_PAGES are both read. tree_diff's three-way classification is not speculative: the DeterminismTests case asserts all three arms, and the classification is what makes a determinism failure actionable rather than a boolean.

checks.py is roughly half docstring -- page_accounting carries 42 documentation lines over 13 code lines, entity_symbol_join 23 over 14. On any ordinary reading that is prose compensating for code, and it would normally be flagged.

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, 'Verification Discipline' and 'Evidence You Owe Back', which require a guard's demonstrated failure mode and its measured limits to be recorded, together with the g1 handoff's own requirement that 'what these checks do NOT prove is recorded honestly beside each check'.
override.reason: The prose is not describing what the code does -- the code is short and plain enough not to need that. It records what the check CANNOT catch and who owns the gap: StoreScan states that an extractor which never recorded an edge agrees with itself and passes; entity_symbol_join states why it compares leaf names only and that g2 owns D2; page_accounting states why counting the tree a second time is not the fix. Every one of those is a measured limit that would otherwise live only in a run report a later gate never reads, and I verified two of them by attack (A5, and the implementer's own extractor-drops-reads survivor). Deleting this prose would delete the gate's findings, not its deodorant. The standard subordinates the smell.
